uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of displayed physical scale.
additionalSystematics: Usui2011 section2.3 omits unquantified shape, spin and thermal-model effects. Rotation can add a few to about10% in size, especially for few detections; no invented total error bar is assigned.
diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Assigning it as the volume-equivalent diameter of a separate DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published mesh-volume calibration.
limitations: Hanuš2018 Eos-family study TableB.1 reports27 dense lightcurves across six apparitions and304 sparse measurements, model quality3. Both poles remain; model1743 is selected without rejecting1744. That paper’s91.2±2.2 km column is WISE radiometry rather than a shape calibration; it is retained as a competing thermal estimate against AKARI107.74±1.51 km. The disagreement is an additional systematic limit, not grounds for averaging the catalogs. The thermal scale is approximate. Convex inversion supplies broad outline without resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture.
visibleDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 107.74 km effective diameter (catalog ±1.51 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size supplies a volume-scale approximation. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.
